intro: A pattern is a shape in price that has historically leaned one way more often than not. It is a probability, not a promise — the same shape fails regularly. Use it to frame a trade (entry, stop, target), never as the whole reason for one.

groups.title: Reversal patterns (trend is ending)
rows: Neckline = lows between the peaks. Break below it confirms. Target = peak height projected down.
Mirror of the above; break above the neckline.
Confirms on a break of the trough. Volume often lighter on the 2nd peak.
Confirms on a break of the middle peak.
More touches = more decisive, but also a slower break.
Gradual shift in momentum; slow to form, slow to confirm.
Rising wedge in an uptrend warns of a stall; falling wedge in a downtrend of a bounce.

groups.title: Continuation patterns (trend pauses, then resumes)
rows: The pole (sharp move) projects the target from the breakout.
Small symmetrical triangle after a move
Shorter than a flag; breakout in the trend direction.
Buyers stepping up; break of the flat top.
Wait for the break — direction is undecided until then.
Handle should be shallow; break of the handle high.
Trade the edges, or wait for the range break.

detection.hint: Two local highs within ~1% of each other, separated by a trough ≥ ~3%
Three local highs where the middle > both sides by ≥ ~2%, shoulders within ~2%
Price move ≥ ~5% in ≤ 10 bars, then a counter-drift with range < ~half the pole
Highs falling and lows rising (converging) over ≥ 15 bars
Drawdown ≥ ~15% then recovery to near the old high, then a ≤ ~5% dip
lower_wick ≥ 2 x body and upper_wick small
today's body fully covers yesterday's body, opposite colour

discipline: Pattern is a setup, not a signal. Wait for the confirmation break; a pattern that never breaks is not a trade.
Define the stop before the entry — usually the other side of the pattern (neckline, flag low, handle low).
Position size from the stop distance, not from conviction.
Backtest the rule, not the story. Detect the pattern numerically, measure the hit rate on your own archive, and only then trust it.
Most patterns fail. The edge, if any, is in the risk management and the confirmation, not the shape.
Features for a model: build_features.py (returns, SMA ratios, RSI, volatility, volume z-score)
The same detection rules can be added as another feature column, then tested walk-forward — never on a random split.
